rent_increase_limits.question: How much can my rent go up?

effective.derived: New Jersey municipal default: 20 days after final passage 2026-05-20 (N.J.S.A. 40:49-2(d), 40:69A-181(b)); mayoral approval or publication may make it later

answer.reason: It directly addresses the rent amount, though only for substantially reconstructed or rehabilitated dwellings; the other provision is a petition procedure.
answer.requirement: Substantially reconstructed or rehabilitated dwellings are not restricted in the initial rent charged if the Rent Control Board makes the required determinations, including that rehabilitation costs during a twelve-month period exceed 50% of fair market value.
answer.key_value: not restricted in initial rent charged
answer.quote:
Substantially reconstructed or rehabilitated dwellings shall not be restricted in initial rent charged, if the Rent Control Board has made the following determinations: 
a. The Board shall determine that the cost of reconstruction or rehabilitation during a twelve-month period exceeds 50% of the fair market value of the property.

effective.derived: New Jersey municipal default: 20 days after final passage 2024-09-18 (N.J.S.A. 40:49-2(d), 40:69A-181(b)); mayoral approval or publication may make it later

answer.reason: This states the ordinary rent-increase limit at lease expiration: the CPI-based increase, capped at 4%. The 25% figure is only a ceiling on increases the Rent Control Board may grant.
answer.requirement: At lease expiration or termination of a periodic tenant's lease, a landlord may not request or receive an increase above the stated CPI calculation, and the increase may never exceed 4%.
answer.key_value: CPI increase, capped at 4%
answer.quote: At the expiration of a lease or at the termination of the lease of a periodic tenant, no landlord may request or receive an increase greater than the percentage increase in the Consumer Price Index (CPI) from the CPI fifteen (15) months prior to the month of the proposed rent increase to the CPI three (3) months prior to the month of the proposed rent increase. In no case shall the allowable rent increase exceed four (4%) percent.

effective.derived: New Jersey municipal default: 20 days after final passage 2023-08-02 (N.J.S.A. 40:49-2(d), 40:69A-181(b)); mayoral approval or publication may make it later

answer.reason: It is the provision tied directly to rent amounts. The other provision concerns which dwellings are covered, not how much rent may increase.
answer.key_value: Fair market rents as established by the United States Department of Housing and Urban Development

effective.derived: New Jersey municipal default: 20 days after final passage 2017-09-05 (N.J.S.A. 40:49-2(d), 40:69A-181(b)); mayoral approval or publication may make it later

answer.reason: This provision directly concerns how much rent may increase in a year, so it is relevant to the renter’s question.
answer.key_value: 25% in any one year

effective.derived: New Jersey municipal default: 20 days after final passage 2017-03-07 (N.J.S.A. 40:49-2(d), 40:69A-181(b)); mayoral approval or publication may make it later

answer.reason: This is the only provision that states an amount for a rent increase. It is a special rehabilitation-increase limit, not the ordinary annual rule for a normal tenancy.
answer.key_value: Up to 20%

just_cause_eviction.question: When can they end my tenancy?

effective.derived: New Jersey municipal default: 20 days after final passage 2024-09-18 (N.J.S.A. 40:49-2(d), 40:69A-181(b)); mayoral approval or publication may make it later

answer.reason: It directly addresses when a landlord may not bring an action to recover possession. It is only a specific prohibition, not the ordinary rule listing when a tenancy may be ended.
answer.requirement: A landlord may not bring an action to recover possession of a dwelling unit in reprisal for a tenant's efforts to secure or enforce rights under the chapter.
answer.quote: No landlord shall bring any action to recover possession of a dwelling unit as a reprisal for the tenant's efforts to secure or enforce any right under this chapter.

effective.derived: New Jersey municipal default: 20 days after final passage 2017-09-05 (N.J.S.A. 40:49-2(d), 40:69A-181(b)); mayoral approval or publication may make it later

answer.reason: This provision addresses when a landlord may end a tenancy, so it is the relevant ordinary rule for the renter’s question.
